extracted.intended_audience: aspiring novelists and fiction writers planning or outlining novels
extracted.subtask_description: Compare and apply the Save the Cat! 15-beat beat sheet and the Seven Point Story Structure as templates for plotting and outlining a novel; the page explains each beat/point and how they map to one another. Useful for writers creating character arcs and plotting a novel from concept to draft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hero should have three things
rubrics_metrics.description: Before diving into the Save the Cat! Beat sheet, Jessica Brody encourages writers to take some time to flesh out the hero of the story. The hero should have three things: A Problem, A Want, A Need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the hero has these three things, the 15 beats will sketch a path for the hero to transform from who they were at the beginning to who they are at the end of the story (and it keeps that transformation engaging and meaningful to the reader).

rubrics_metrics.name: A Problem — The hero’s flaws
rubrics_metrics.description: These are the aspects about them that will transform during the arc of a character’s development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They can be intrinsic flaws (a source of conflict from within the hero) or extrinsic flaws (a setback forced upon the hero).

rubrics_metrics.name: A Want — The hero’s goals
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the A story or the story’s premise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is the exciting problem that the reader is hoping will be solved by the end of the story.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Need — The lesson to be learned
rubrics_metrics.description: This is the B-story, otherwise thought of as the moral of the story or what the story is really about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Need often underpins the character's internal change and is revealed through the B-story/helper character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-act structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Save the Cat! and the Seven Point Story Structure utilize a three act structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post treats both templates as three-act based frameworks and maps beats/points into that overarching structure; use either as an organizing scaffold for beginning/middle/end plotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening Image
rubrics_metrics.description: That status of the character at the beginning of the story, this should oppose the final image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets tone and shows who the hero is before the arc; serves as a foil to the Final Image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theme Stated
rubrics_metrics.description: A subtle allusion to what the story is really about.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be understated and hint at the moral or central idea that will be explored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-Up
rubrics_metrics.description: Shows the hero living in their opening status, it illustrates their flaws in examples of their work, home, and social life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes normal world and the hero's routine and weaknesses so later change is meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catalyst
rubrics_metrics.description: Often thought of as the inciting incident. It is a moment/event that disrupts how the hero lives in their world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An external event that propels the hero toward change; should clearly disrupt the status quo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Debate
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero is resistant to the change that has to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows hesitation and internal conflict about embarking on the journey; dramatizes stakes and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break into Two
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero can no longer fight it; it is now time to begin their journey of change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks transition from Act One to Act Two — the hero commits (or is forced) into the new situation.

rubrics_metrics.name: B Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduces a helper character that will assist the hero in discovering the theme and eventually what they really need.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often carries the moral/relationship arc that helps the protagonist learn their Need; can be romantic, mentor, or friend relationship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fun and Games
rubrics_metrics.description: The promise of the premise, this is all the tension-filled action and adventure that the hero will encounter on their journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typically where the main concept of the story is explored — delivers the pleasures of the premise while still advancing plot and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midpoint
rubrics_metrics.description: Either a false victory or a false failure. The A storyline and B storyline will co-mingle and the stakes will be raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A turning moment that changes the direction or urgency of the story; often increases stakes or changes the protagonist’s approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bad Guys Close In
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar to fun and games, it is how the hero will recover after the midpoint before reaching their lowest point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Antagonistic forces intensify; pressure mounts and the hero’s weaknesses are exploited.

rubrics_metrics.name: All Is Lost
rubrics_metrics.description: The lowest point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The moment when it seems everything has been lost — often coincides with a symbolic 'whiff of death' or definitive setback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dark Night of the Soul
rubrics_metrics.description: How a character reacts to their lowest point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reflective moment of despair or reckoning that precedes the character's epiphany and decision to act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Break into Three
rubrics_metrics.description: The epiphany moment where the hero understands what they have to do to fix their problem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transition into Act Three — protagonist synthesizes lessons (often from B Story) and formulates a plan for the finale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finale
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero puts their plan into action and leads to the climax.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sequence where the protagonist enacts change, confronts antagonists, and resolves the main conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Image
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero at the end of the story, should have changed significantly from who they were at the beginning of the story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides emotional payoff and shows the completed character arc in contrast to the Opening Image.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hook (Seven Point) — Opening Image/Theme Stated/Set up
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the character starts at the beginning (should heavily oppose where they are at the end).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines opening elements to firmly establish the protagonist's starting point and set up contrast for the arc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Turn 1 (Seven Point) — Catalyst/Debate/Break into 2
rubrics_metrics.description: This will be an event that sets the story into motion. The main conflict is introduced and the hero embarks on their journey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functions as the inciting incident/decision that propels the protagonist from setup into the main plot.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinch Point 1 (Seven Point) — B story/Fun & Games
rubrics_metrics.description: There is tension added and often the antagonist is introduced (or does something devious).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pressure point that reminds the reader of the stakes and the presence of antagonistic forces mid-Act Two.

rubrics_metrics.name: Midpoint (Seven Point)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of being reactive, the midpoint encourages the hero to become more active. Something must be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A shift from reaction to action; raises stakes and forces a change in protagonist's approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pinch Point 2 (Seven Point) — Bad Guys Closing in/All is Lost/Dark Night of the Soul
rubrics_metrics.description: The stakes have never been higher. The character is at the darkest moment or has lost everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Second pressure point that drives the protagonist to their nadir and sets up the eventual turn toward resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Turn 2 (Seven Point) — Break into Three
rubrics_metrics.description: The main character starts to move toward the resolution. They now understand what they have to do to achieve what they set out to do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The epiphany/decision that propels the hero into Act Three with a clear plan informed by lessons learned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution (Seven Point) — Finale/Final image
rubrics_metrics.description: The hero reaches the climax. They will either win or lose at this moment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivers the story’s climax and shows the protagonist's transformation as the conflict resolves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Save the Cat! beat sheet as a checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: The Save the Cat! beat sheet is invaluable to the author as a checklist to ensure they’re setting their story up for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the 15 beats as a way to verify key story moments are present and that the character arc is properly scaffolded, rather than as an inflexible formula.
